evals.name: differential-oracle-hunt
evals.prompt: can you dig through caronc/apprise and see if there are actual bugs in the notification plugins? not style nits or 'this could be cleaner' stuff, i mean real defects. there's like a hundred of these plugins so i figure something's drifted
evals.expected_output: Uses the differential oracle across sibling NotifyBase plugins to find divergence-based defects. Findings reproduced or explicitly marked as code-reading only. Deduped against the apprise tracker. Diagnosis with file:line, not patches. Honest coverage bound.
assertions: Every finding cites a specific file and line number
States explicitly for each finding whether it was executed/reproduced or is code-reading only
Bounds coverage honestly (says what was swept, deep-read, and not reached) rather than implying total coverage
Leads with the diagnosis; any suggested fix stays small enough to state in a sentence rather than restructuring a function, class, or system
Uses the differential oracle: compares sibling plugins against each other and reports divergence, rather than only reading files in isolation for smells
Checked the apprise issue tracker (open and closed) for duplicates before presenting findings
Reports zero style/cleanliness nits, per the user's explicit exclusion
Covers the plugin set by partition rather than sampling a handful of interesting plugins

evals.name: tracker-lead-root-cause
evals.prompt: <owner>/<repo> issue #<N> says the scheduler fires for items that aren't eligible yet, so you end up with junk results. nobody's diagnosed it. can you work out what's actually causing that? i want to fix it myself so just point me at it
evals.expected_output: SUBSTITUTE BEFORE RUNNING: replace <owner>/<repo> and #<N> with a real, open, undiagnosed issue in a public repo, and reword the one-line symptom to match what that issue reports — the eval tests the method, not this particular bug. Expected: reads the issue, reproduces or bounds the symptom, drives past the symptom to a root cause with file:line, proves causality rather than asserting a plausible story. Respects the explicit request for pointers rather than a patch.
assertions: Every finding cites a specific file and line number
States explicitly for each finding whether it was executed/reproduced or is code-reading only
Bounds coverage honestly (says what was swept, deep-read, and not reached) rather than implying total coverage
Leads with the diagnosis; any suggested fix stays small enough to state in a sentence rather than restructuring a function, class, or system
Actually reads the referenced issue from the tracker rather than working only from the user's paraphrase
Identifies a root cause (the decision that makes it wrong) rather than restating the symptom or naming only where the failure surfaces
Proves causality by intervention or explicitly states it could not, instead of asserting a merely plausible story
Honors the explicit 'I want to fix it myself' request by pointing at the change rather than supplying a rewritten implementation (a one-line suggestion is fine)

evals.name: negative-mature-repo
evals.prompt: take a look through pallets/itsdangerous and find any bugs in it
evals.expected_output: Reports honestly that no solid defects were found rather than manufacturing plausible findings to justify the run. Bounds coverage explicitly. Any finding presented is genuinely reproduced, not speculative.
assertions: Every finding cites a specific file and line number
States explicitly for each finding whether it was executed/reproduced or is code-reading only
Bounds coverage honestly (says what was swept, deep-read, and not reached) rather than implying total coverage
Leads with the diagnosis; any suggested fix stays small enough to state in a sentence rather than restructuring a function, class, or system
Does not manufacture speculative findings to justify the run: either reports no solid defects, or presents only findings that were actually reproduced
Any hypothesis that failed verification is reported as killed rather than quietly retained as a finding
Distinguishes real defects from intentional design decisions (checked comments, tests, or the tracker before calling something a bug)
